newsitem.title: USA: Higher Thai 97/98 corn, wheat imports - US attache.
newsitem.headline: Higher Thai 97/98 corn, wheat imports - US attache.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache forecast Thailand's corn imports would climb to 500,000 tonnes in marketing year 1997/98 due to stagnant domestic production and rising consumption.

In a report dated March 20 released here Wednesday, the attache pegged Thai 1996/97 corn imports at 200,000 tonnes, below a prior estimate, "due mainly to uncertainty surrounding the Thai import policy and relatively competitive prices for domestic corn."
The attache said Argentine corn poses a threat to U.S. market share because of its color preference, cleaner grains and cheaper prices.

On wheat, the attache forecast total 1997/98 imports at 750,000 tonnes and said the U.S. should continue to capture 35-40 percent of market share in 1997/98 due to a change in market demand toward use of U.S. wheat.
